title: Acute Ischemic Stroke — Time-Based Algorithm
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Stroke / TIA (AHA 2023)

2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke. Stroke. 2026 (AHA/ASA) — Class 2a recommendation for 4.5–9 h / wake-up stroke thrombolysis with advanced-imaging selection; endorses tenecteplase as equivalent to alteplase across the 4.5 h window.
Key supporting trials for the extended window: TRACE-III, EXTEND, WAKE-UP.
AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke (2019, 2023 update); DAWN, DEFUSE-3

changelog.change: Currency update: replaced the vague 'HOPE trial' wake-up-stroke mention with the actual 2026 AHA/ASA guideline position — a new Class 2a recommendation for IV thrombolysis 4.5–9 h post-onset or wake-up stroke with advanced-imaging (DWI-FLAIR or perfusion mismatch) selection, sourced to TRACE-III/EXTEND/WAKE-UP. Also updated the tenecteplase line: the 2026 guideline endorses it as equivalent to alteplase across the full 4.5 h window, not only as a pre-thrombectomy convenience.
Added whyThisMatters + clinicalTakeaway (standard Reference Library template, DIRECTIONS_FORWARD §1).
Initial entry — the time-anchored workup, IV thrombolysis dosing + BP targets + contraindications, the thrombectomy window, and ICH management targets.

summary: Time = brain (~1.9 million neurons/min in a large-vessel occlusion). Non-contrast CT first to exclude hemorrhage. IV thrombolysis within 4.5 h if eligible (BP must be < 185/110 first). CT angiography for LVO → thrombectomy, up to 24 h with perfusion-imaging selection.
whyThisMatters: Large-vessel occlusion destroys around 1.9 million neurons a minute, so every step of the workup is a race — and the two irreversible errors are giving thrombolysis into an unrecognized hemorrhage, or missing an LVO that a thrombectomy could still reopen up to 24 hours out.
clinicalTakeaway: Non-contrast CT first to exclude blood. If eligible, give IV thrombolysis within 4.5 hours — but get the BP below 185/110 first. Get CT angiography on anyone with a plausible LVO and move them toward thrombectomy, using perfusion imaging to select out to 24 hours.

items: 0–25 min: NIHSS, fingerstick glucose, INR / anti-Xa if on anticoagulation, ECG, weight → STAT non-contrast head CT. Do not delay CT for labs unless anticoagulation is known/suspected.

25–45 min (if eligible): IV thrombolysis — alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg), 10% as a bolus over 1 min, the rest over 60 min — for onset (or last-known-well) within 4.5 h. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline now endorses tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg single IV bolus as an equally acceptable alternative to alteplase across the whole 4.5 h window, not just as a pre-thrombectomy convenience — a single bolus with no infusion pump is the practical advantage.
0–24 h, large-vessel occlusion: CT angiography → mechanical thrombectomy. Standard window 0–6 h; extend to 24 h with DAWN / DEFUSE-3 perfusion-mismatch criteria.

Extended-window thrombolysis (4.5–9 h, or wake-up stroke with unknown onset): new Class 2a recommendation in the 2026 AHA/ASA guideline — IV thrombolysis (alteplase or tenecteplase) may be reasonable in this window if advanced imaging (MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch, or CT/MR perfusion mismatch) shows salvageable brain tissue, based on TRACE-III, EXTEND, and WAKE-UP. This is now a guideline-level recommendation, not just a perfusion-imaging option to consider — involve the stroke team early for imaging selection rather than defaulting to 'outside the window, no thrombolysis' past 4.5 h.

Before thrombolysis: must be < 185 / 110 — treat with labetalol 10–20 mg IV or a nicardipine / clevidipine infusion. If it can't be brought and held below that safely, thrombolysis is contraindicated.

No thrombolysis (permissive hypertension): allow up to 220 / 120 unless another indication to treat (aortic dissection, ACS, acute HF, hypertensive encephalopathy) — over-aggressive lowering extends the infarct.

Absolute: hemorrhage on CT; prior ICH; serious head trauma / intracranial surgery / ischemic stroke within 3 months; active internal bleeding; platelets < 100k; INR > 1.7 or elevated PT; therapeutic LMWH within 24 h; a direct thrombin or factor-Xa inhibitor within 48 h (unless coagulation tests are normal); BP that stays > 185 / 110 despite treatment; blood glucose < 50 not corrected; suspected infective endocarditis / aortic dissection.
Extended-window (3–4.5 h) additional relative contraindications: age > 80, NIHSS > 25, any anticoagulant use (any dose / INR), a history of BOTH prior stroke AND diabetes.
The list is guideline-specific and evolving — check the current AHA/ASA table and involve the stroke team; many former absolute contraindications are now relative.

body.text: Intracerebral hemorrhage (if the CT shows blood)

rows: SBP to ~ 140 mmHg (acceptable range often 130–150) — rapid, smooth lowering; avoid dropping below 130
4F-PCC 25–50 U/kg + vitamin K 10 mg IV slow; target INR < 1.4
4F-PCC 25–50 U/kg (andexanet withdrawn from the US market 2025-12) — see the anticoagulation-reversal module

Head of bed 30°, head midline; mannitol 0.5–1 g/kg or hypertonic saline; brief hyperventilation only if actively herniating; neurosurgery for a posterior-fossa bleed, hydrocephalus, or a large lobar/deep bleed
